extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students in algebraic topology; mathematicians learning homology and cohomology
extracted.subtask_description: Study and apply core algebraic topology results: transfer sequences for coverings, simplicial approximation, Lefschetz fixed point theorem, constructions of simplicial mapping cylinders/cones, and basic cohomology (cochains, coboundary δ, cup product idea).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer sequence for a 2-sheeted covering (transfer homomorphism τ*, p*)
rubrics_metrics.description: The long exact sequence in homology associated to the short exact sequence of chain complexes coming from a 2-sheeted covering p: X̃ → X with maps τ (inclusion of lifts) and p♯ (projection). Using Z2 coefficients the kernel of p♯ is generated by sums σ1 + σ2 of the two lifts of a simplex, τ is injective, and τ∗ and p∗ give the resulting long exact 'transfer' sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: each singular simplex in X lifts to two simplices in X̃, kernel of p♯ described by σ1+σ2; short exact sequence of chain complexes yields long exact sequence in homology. Remarks: τ∗ is a special case of general transfer homomorphisms and relates to Gysin sequences; generalization to other coefficients requires local coefficients. Practical use: compute homology of RP^n with Z2 coefficients and analyze induced maps under quotient maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Odd self-map of S^n has odd degree (use of transfer sequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: An odd map f: S^n → S^n (f(−x) = −f(x)) induces maps on the transfer sequence for the covering S^n → RP^n, and naturality/commutativity of the transfer diagram shows f∗ on H_n(S^n; Z2) is an isomorphism, hence its degree is odd (degree mod 2 = 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: check commutativity of squares (pf = fp and lifts behave antipodally), use induction on dimension and the fact that in a commutative square if three maps are isomorphisms the fourth is too. Lemma used: degree mod 2 equals action on top homology with Z2 coefficients. Minor cases (n=1) handled separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borsuk–Ulam theorem (corollary via odd maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any map g: S^n → R^n there exists x ∈ S^n with g(x) = g(−x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: form f(x) = g(x) − g(−x), which is odd; if f never zero normalize to map S^n → S^{n−1} and restrict to equator to get an odd map with nonzero degree contradiction via previous proposition. Use the odd-degree result to force a zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicial Approximation Theorem (Theorem 2C.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K is a finite simplicial complex and L any simplicial complex, any continuous map f: K → L is homotopic to a simplicial map after sufficiently many barycentric subdivisions of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof ingredients: choose metric on K, Lebesgue number for cover {st w | w vertex of L}, subdivide K so stars have small diameter, define g on vertices by ensuring f(St v) ⊂ st g(v), extend to simplices using Lemma 2C.2 (nonempty intersection of open stars implies image vertices form simplex), and construct homotopy by linear paths inside simplices. Remarks: can make approximation close if subdividing L too; can keep fixed vertices where f already sends vertices to vertices (useful for basepoint preservation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2C.2 (intersection of open stars)
rubrics_metrics.description: For vertices v1,...,vn of a simplicial complex X, st v1 ∩ ... ∩ st vn is empty unless v1,...,vn are vertices of a simplex σ of X, in which case the intersection equals st σ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use: key combinatorial lemma used to check that the chosen vertex images g(v) extend to a simplicial map on each simplex (nonempty intersection of their stars implies they are vertices of a simplex in target). Proof: intersection consists of interiors of simplices whose vertex sets contain {v1,...,vn}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of star and open star
rubrics_metrics.description: Star St σ of simplex σ is the subcomplex consisting of simplices containing σ; open star st σ is union of interiors of simplices containing σ (open set whose closure is St σ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role: used to localize f and choose vertex images in simplicial approximation (ensure f(St v) ⊂ st g(v)). Also used in arguments controlling diameters and homotopies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lefschetz number and Lefschetz Fixed Point Theorem (Theorem 2C.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a map f: X → X of a finite simplicial complex (or retract of one) with finitely generated homology vanishing in high dimensions, the Lefschetz number τ(f) = Σ_n (−1)^n tr(f∗: H_n(X) → H_n(X)). If τ(f) ≠ 0 then f has a fixed point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: reduce to finite simplicial complexes, assume no fixed points to derive τ(f)=0 by simplicial approximation producing simplicial g homotopic to f with g(σ) ∩ σ = ∅ for each simplex σ; compute τ(g) via traces on cellular chain groups H_n(K_n, K_{n−1}) where diagonal entries vanish when g(σ) ∩ σ = ∅, use additivity of trace on short exact sequences. Remarks: compactness and local contractibility hypotheses are essential (counterexamples exist otherwise). Examples and applications: projective spaces, linear maps → fixed eigenvectors, examples showing parity phenomena for real/complex/projective/quaternionic cases; τ(id)=χ(X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace additivity in exact sequences (algebraic fact used in Lefschetz)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commutative diagram with exact rows A→B→C and endomorphisms α,β,γ compatible with the diagram, tr(β) = tr(α) + tr(γ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: reduce to case of free modules by factoring/taking torsion into account and possibly enlarging subgroups; used to pass from traces on relative cellular homology groups to traces on absolute homology in Lefschetz computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of simplicial mapping cylinder M(f) and simplicial mapping cone C(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a simplicial map f: K → L, construct a simplicial complex M(f) containing L and the barycentric subdivision K′ as subcomplexes and deformation retracting onto L with r1|_{K′} = f; then C(f) obtained by attaching cone on K′ to K′ ⊂ M(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction proceeds simplex-by-simplex: build M(f|_{K_{n}}) inductively by coning extensions M(f|_{∂σ} → τ) to get M(f|_{σ} → τ). Show each attachment is contractible and arrange deformation retractions iteratively (concatenate over t-intervals). Use homotopy extension property to adjust retraction so r1|_{K}=f. Application: used in Theorem 2C.5 to attach cells simplicially and realize CW complexes by simplicial complexes up to homotopy.

rubrics_metrics.name: CW complexes are homotopy equivalent to simplicial complexes (Theorem 2C.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every CW complex X is homotopy equivalent to a simplicial complex Y of the same dimension; Y can be finite if X is finite and countable if X is countable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: inductively build simplicial Yn homotopy equivalent to X^n and CW Zn deformation retracting onto X^n and Yn; for each attaching map S^n → X^n use simplicial approximation to replace with simplicial map f and attach simplicial mapping cones C(f) to extend Yn to Yn+1; glue in cylinders to keep homotopy equivalence to X. Remarks: mapping cylinder/cone machinery avoids awkwardness of simplicial mapping cones in naive form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology via cochains and coboundary δ (definitions and low-dimensional interpretations)
rubrics_metrics.description: C^i(X; G) = functions from i-simplices (or vertices/edges) to abelian group G; coboundary δ: C^0 → C^1 given by δϕ([v0,v1]) = ϕ(v1)−ϕ(v0); cohomology H^i(X;G) = Ker δ / Im δ. In low dimensions: H^0(X;G) = functions constant on components; H^1(X;G) measures obstructions to solving δϕ = ψ (analogy to gradient and curl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graph interpretation: for a tree δϕ=ψ always solvable given basepoint; for a general graph values on edges not in a maximal tree give independent degrees of freedom so H^1 ≅ product of copies of G indexed by edges not in maximal tree. For 2-complexes, δ on 1-cochains to 2-cochains measures additivity deviations on triangles; δδ=0 so local obstruction δψ=0 is necessary for ψ to be δ of a 0-cochain, and nontrivial class in H^1 is a global obstruction. Geometric viewpoint for surfaces with G=Z2: δψ=0 corresponds to curves crossing edges with even intersection counts and relates to decompositions into regions when ψ=δϕ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cup product idea via cross product and diagonal map
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohomology admits a natural product (cup product) because contravariance gives maps in the opposite direction: use the cross product H^i(X) × H^j(X) → H^{i+j}(X×X) together with the diagonal map Δ: X → X×X (x ↦ (x,x)) to obtain H^{i+j}(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with homology: while there is a cross product Hi(X)×Hj(X)→H_{i+j}(X×X), there's no natural map X×X→X for general X so no analogous product in homology (except for H-spaces via Pontryagin product). Cup product produces ring structure on cohomology, and this extra algebraic structure is central for further results (e.g., Poincaré duality, characteristic classes).
